pairs.why: Both keep the same orange roof, yellow body, brown trunk and green park, with no hue or chroma gap that favors one.
Both use the same lime green instead of the real emerald and the same saturated orange dunes, so the palette gap is equal.
Both add an orange striped wall and a more orange floor than the real desaturated tan wood, and both have a similar teal plate and fruit palette.
B keeps navy keys with cyan operators, matching the real navy and cyan body, while A adds off-palette beige keys as an extra hue family.
Both show the same pinkish-grey stone, navy and cream board, and saturated green grass with a blue sky the real card lacks.
B's soles are nearer the real coral-orange and its flat cyan stripes lean closer to the real teal-mint, while A goes crimson-red on deeper electric blue with a bright glow.
Both have the same pink-magenta body with cyan glow, coral tentacles and brighter blue background than the real deep indigo.
A's muted brown floor keeps the orange pumpkin as the one hot hue against purple, while B's orange wood merges with the pumpkin and pulls the card warm.
